pr_title: Fix 500 when a comment was deleted which has a notification
pr_comments:
I think this is just going to push the problem up higher in the stack and cause an npe.

There's lots of the notification code that assumes that comment has to be there instead of protecting against a missing comment.

> I think this is just going to push the problem up higher in the stack and cause an npe.
> 
> There's lots of the notification code that assumes that comment has to be there instead of protecting against a missing comment.

All notification to the comments of one issue in fact should be merged to last comment(current logic in Gitea's code), so the comment_id on the notification is not very meaningful.

> There's lots of the notification code that assumes that comment has to be there instead of protecting against a missing comment.

I should add that I meant the API notification code here. The UI does the right thing.

There's lots of places in the API where the comment is assumed to be present and it would take a bit of thought to double check and ensure that the dropping the comment is reasonable or if it needs some other flag.
I've added a few other places we can ignore the error too.

issue_context.title: [API] notifcations API returns 500 if comment was deleted
issue_context.body:
### Gitea Version

1.16.0

### How are you running Gitea?

built from source, from cli

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

Yes

### Description

The notifications API (`api/v1/notifications`) returns a 500 internal server error if any notification addresses a comment that was deleted.
`...pi/v1/notify/user.go:85:ListNotifications() [E] InternalServerError: GetCommentByID [193] for issue ID [53]: comment does not exist [id: 193, issue_id: 0]`
comments: OK so the problem here is that `NotificationList.LoadAttributes()` is not fault tolerant and will return whenever there is an error.

review_comments: Isn't it already an `ErrCommentNotExist` in this case? Why construct a new error instead of simply omitting this case then?
The old error only include commentID, here we added issueID
